title: Bernard Shaw's Funeral: The Animals' Procession
culture_region: India / Greece / USA / South Africa / World
summary: Refusing meat even when warned by doctors in extreme old age, Shaw joked that his funeral cortege would be led by weeping herds of sheep, cattle, and poultry grateful he never ate them.
keywords: Bernard Shaw's Funeral: The Animals' Procession
full_text:
George Bernard Shaw was an ardent, uncompromising vegetarian from age twenty-five until his death at ninety-four. He famously described carnivorism as 'cannibalism with its heroic dish omitted.'

In his ninetieth year, a physician urged him to consume beef broth to regain physical vitality.

Shaw looked at the doctor with playful defiance:
"Doctor, my body is a temple of life, not a graveyard for the corpses of murdered beasts!
Do you know why I refuse to touch your meat?
Because I have already choreographed my funeral procession!

When my hearse rolls through the streets, it will not be followed by mourning politicians or critics.
It will be followed by vast herds of cattle, sheep, pigs, and flocks of poultry and fish!
They will all be wearing black armbands, weeping tears of gratitude, and shouting:
'Behold the noble man who passed through life without devouring a single one of us!'
Would you deprive me of such a magnificent funeral, Doctor?"

The physician conceded defeat. Shaw lived vigorously into his ninety-fifth year, championing compassion for all living beings with boundless wit.
moral: Ethical living requires extending empathy beyond our own species to all sentient life on earth.
